title: 14 — Hands-On Build Plan: Ten Phases
html:
14 — Hands-On Build Plan: Ten Phases

The one idea: learn the whole stack by building it once, end to end, on a laptop with free tools — each phase produces something that runs, and each phase uses only what the previous phases built. Use fictional or openly licensed sample data throughout.

1. The target architecture

---
title: End-to-end financial lakehouse and agent architecture
---
flowchart TB
    subgraph ING["1. Ingestion and document intelligence"]
        SRC["Sources: websites, PDFs, CSV, SFTP, CDC, streams"] --> REG["Source and rights register"]
        REG --> COL["Unified collector"]
        COL --> LAND["Immutable landing<br/>SHA-256 + Object Lock"]
        LAND --> DOC["Document AI<br/>layout, OCR, entities, sentiment"]
        DOC --> GATE["Quality gate<br/>(data contracts)"]
        GATE -->|fail| QUA["Quarantine"]
    end
    subgraph LH["2. Bitemporal lakehouse"]
        GATE -->|pass| BR["Bronze to Silver<br/>Iceberg + Parquet"]
        BR --> ER["Entity resolution<br/>and relationship graph"]
        ER --> HUM["Maker-checker certification"]
        HUM --> GOLD["Gold: certified, tagged vintages"]
    end
    subgraph AI["3. Serving and agents"]
        GOLD --> SEM["Semantic metric views (DuckDB)"]
        GOLD --> IDX["Hybrid search index"]
        SEM --> MCP["MCP server: deterministic tools"]
        IDX --> MCP
        MCP --> GW["AI gateway"]
        GW --> RT["Agent runtime<br/>(8-step turn)"]
        RT --> UI["Web UI"]
    end

2. The ten phases

Phase Build Local stack Chapters
1 Infrastructure and WORM storage Docker Compose, MinIO, PostgreSQL, REST catalog 03, 07
2 Document intelligence worker Docling, PaddleOCR, GLiNER, FinBERT, Pydantic 02, 11
3 Quality and conformance gate datacontract-cli, Polars, DuckDB, Pydantic 08
4 Bitemporal Iceberg lakehouse PyIceberg, DuckDB, MinIO 05, 06, 09
5 Entity resolution and relationship graph Splink, RapidFuzz, NetworkX, Polars 10
6 Human assurance workbench and maker-checker PostgreSQL, Flowable, FastAPI or Spring, Iceberg tags 09, 13
7 Risk analytics and hybrid search index Qdrant or pgvector, NetworkX, Polars, MLflow 12
8 Semantic serving and MCP server DuckDB, FastMCP / MCP SDK, FastAPI 02, 12
9 AI gateway and guardrails LiteLLM, Ollama, Redis, MLflow tracing 12
10 Agent runtime and web UI Java 21, Spring Boot 3, SPI, OpenFeign, RAGAS, Angular/React or .NET 13

3. Phase by phase

Phase 1 — Infrastructure and WORM storage

  1. Write compose.yaml with MinIO, PostgreSQL 16, a REST catalog (Lakekeeper or Polaris) and Redis.
  2. Create buckets: landing with Object Lock (Compliance, e.g. 7 years in production, 1 day while experimenting), warehouse without.
  3. Create the source_register and acquisition_manifest tables in PostgreSQL.
  4. Write a collector with one HTTP adapter that downloads a public daily file, hashes it and lands it.

Done when: running the collector twice lands the file once and records a duplicate delivery; a delete attempt leaves the locked version intact.

Phase 2 — Document intelligence worker

  1. Pick 5 public annual reports or factsheets (or create fictional PDFs).
  2. Run Docling; export tables to DataFrames and keep page_no + bbox for each.
  3. OCR scanned pages with PaddleOCR; normalise coordinates.
  4. Extract 10 target fields into a Pydantic model; run GLiNER for auditor names, pledges, covenant breaches; FinBERT on auditor's report paragraphs.
  5. Write bronze.extracted_value rows.

Done when: every extracted value has file hash, page, bbox, extractor version and confidence.

Phase 3 — Quality and conformance gate

  1. Write ODCS contracts for two Bronze datasets.
  2. Implement structural, schema, range, uniqueness, drift and cross-source checks as rules in a table.
  3. Route failures to a PostgreSQL quarantine table; publish passes in one commit.
  4. Add datacontract lint to CI.

Done when: a deliberately broken file is quarantined with rule IDs, and a good file publishes atomically with a quality card.

Phase 4 — Bitemporal Iceberg lakehouse

  1. Create bronze, silver, gold namespaces and tables with PyIceberg (explicit schemas, month partitioning, sort order).
  2. Implement the append-only bitemporal event table and the known_to view.
  3. Load an initial value, a correction and a restatement for one fact.
  4. Run the four standard as-of queries in DuckDB.

Done when: the three-answers example from chapter 09 reproduces exactly.

Phase 5 — Entity resolution and relationship graph

  1. Build the canonical entity table and entity_identifier table.
  2. Tier 1 exact matching; Tier 2 Splink with blocking; send the middle band to a review queue.
  3. Load ownership, director, auditor and lender edges bitemporally; build a NetworkX graph for a date.
  4. Implement corroboration scoring and survivorship rules.

Done when: a labelled sample shows precision above your target, and the graph answers "who is within two hops of this issuer?".

Phase 6 — Human assurance workbench and maker-checker

  1. A web page: exception queue, PDF viewer with bounding-box highlight next to the value, accept/correct/reject.
  2. A Flowable (or simple state-machine) process for certifying a Silver snapshot to Gold.
  3. On approval, create the Iceberg tag vintage_YYYY_MM_DD and store a signed digest.

Done when: the maker cannot approve their own release, and the tag reads back the approved data after later loads.

Phase 7 — Risk analytics and hybrid search index

  1. From Gold only: compute simple early-warning indicators (leverage trend, interest cover, restatement count, auditor change, pledge level) and contagion exposure from the graph.
  2. Chunk Gold documents; index in Qdrant or pgvector with dense + sparse vectors and full provenance metadata.
  3. Log experiments and indicator versions in MLflow.

Done when: a search for an exact term and a paraphrase both find the right page, filtered by entitlement.

Phase 8 — Semantic serving and MCP server

  1. Define metric views in DuckDB (metric_as_of(entity, metric, period, as_of)).
  2. Expose get_certified_metric, resolve_entity, compare_restatements as MCP tools and as an entitlement-checked REST API.

Done when: an MCP client can answer "net worth of entity X for FY26 as certified on 31 Oct" with vintage and source.

Phase 9 — AI gateway and guardrails

  1. Run LiteLLM proxy with a local model via Ollama and one frontier model.
  2. Add redaction of personal identifiers, per-key budgets, a kill switch and routing rules.
  3. Turn on MLflow tracing for every call.

Done when: a request with a PAN in it reaches the model masked, and exceeding a budget blocks further calls.

Phase 10 — Agent runtime and web UI

  1. Spring Boot 3 application with the eight-step turn pipeline and SPI-loaded modules.
  2. Stream steps and answer to the UI over SSE.
  3. Build a RAGAS evaluation set and fail the build on faithfulness regressions.

Done when: a question flows through all eight steps, the answer cites pages and vintage, and the trace shows every tool call.

4. Suggested schedule

Weeks Phases Focus
1–2 Chapters 01–02, Phase 1 Domain, Python data stack, storage
3–4 Chapters 03–07, Phase 4 (start) Lakehouse and Iceberg — the core
5 Chapters 08–09, Phases 3–4 Contracts, quality, bitemporal
6 Chapter 11, Phase 2 Documents
7 Chapter 10, Phase 5–6 Entities, graphs, certification
8–9 Chapter 12, Phases 7–9 Retrieval, MCP, gateway
10 Chapter 13, Phase 10 Agent runtime and UI

Building phase 4 before phase 2 is fine: it lets you learn Iceberg with clean CSV data first.

5. Review checklist for the finished build

  • Every Gold number traces back to a landed file, page and bounding box.
  • Every Silver fact is bitemporal; restatements are visible as their own events.
  • Every certified release is a signed Iceberg tag approved by two people.
  • The agent never states a number not returned by a tool.
  • All model calls pass through the gateway with redaction and budgets.
  • Evaluation and data-contract checks run in CI.
